newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cocoa price falls fail to entice German buyers.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa price falls fail to entice German buyers.

text.p: German chocolate manufacturers used lower futures levels to buy some nearby semi-finished cocoa products, but continued to shun physical bean markets, traders said on Wednesday.
"Consumers bought some nearby cocoa powder and butter but are staying out of beans where they could do with some 1997 purchases," one said.
"But they won't move in a falling market when the crop picture in West Africa is beginning to look very comfortable and harvest news may put more pressure on futures," he added.
Traders said semis sales for the Christmas season production had been strong, pointing to good ordering from the chocolate wholesale trade.
"It won't be a bad year for chocolate at all, especially with a cool and wet summer, when more chocolate was sold and finished product stocks were drawn down," another trader said.
"But it's done little for the cocoa bean trade."

Market speculation focused on the Ivory Coast 1996/97 main crop forecast but traders said they found the range attributed to U.S. forecaster Hans Kilian of 790,000-930,000 in recent market talk unhelpful.
"It's too wide for us to work with it," one trader said.
Ivorian beans were quoted at 2.24-2.25 marks per kg for 1996 dates compared with 2.30-2.33 marks a week ago.
The cocoa butter ratio was boosted by two points to 2.80 because of recent buying, which implied mark prices of 6.42 marks for 1996 dates, liquid, ex-works.
The first quarter 1997 ratio of 2.73 implied a mark price of 6.27.
